meta.title: Support — GitKittie
meta.description: Support and troubleshooting for GitKittie Folder, GitKittie Tasks, GitKittie Bud and GitKittie Mail. Most issues come down to access: a git token, a repository URL, folder permissions, or a mail account's password.

title: Support
intro: GitKittie Folder, GitKittie Tasks, GitKittie Bud and GitKittie Mail are small, local-first apps. Most issues come down to access: git, a token, a repository URL, folder permissions, or a mail account's password. Pick your app below.

steps.title: Verify Git is installed
steps.desc: Open Terminal and run `git --version`. If not found, install Xcode Command Line Tools: `xcode-select --install`.

steps.title: Test GitHub access
steps.desc: Open GitKittie Folder Settings, paste a fine-grained GitHub token, enter the repository URL, and run Test GitHub Access.

steps.title: Check the repository URL
steps.desc: Make sure the URL in GitKittie Folder matches the HTTPS URL on your GitHub repository page. It should start with `https://github.com/`. SSH URLs are available under Advanced settings.

items.title: Folder shows "Error" status
items.desc: Open Settings and check the error message. The most common causes are a missing token, a token without repository access, an incorrect repository URL, or a folder permission that needs to be refreshed.

items.title: Folder shows "Needs attention"
items.desc: Open Settings and read the specific recovery message. If a Git operation was interrupted or the branch became detached, use Repair & Sync. File conflicts still need review in your preferred Git client.

items.title: Changes not appearing on GitHub
items.desc: Check that the folder isn't paused and the repository URL and branch are correct. Sync Now fetches remote changes before committing and pushing local changes.

items.title: A file is too large to sync
items.desc: GitHub rejects individual files at or above 100 MB. GitKittie Folder lists the affected paths before staging and can add them to .gitignore while leaving the files on your Mac.

tasks.heading: GitKittie Tasks
tasks.title: Getting connected
tasks.body: GitKittie Tasks is on the Mac App Store and the App Store for iPhone and iPad — one record, so the download button gives you the build for the device you're on. Open the demo board to try it without an account, or connect GitHub, GitLab.com or a self-hosted GitLab. If a repository doesn't show up, check that the token you pasted has repository read and write scope, and that self-hosted GitLab was given its server URL. If live updates won't turn on, your account needs admin access to the repository on GitHub, or the Maintainer role on GitLab. Anything else — a board that won't load, a card that won't save, an agent that can't connect — send a message and it lands against GitKittie Tasks.

bud.heading: GitKittie Bud
bud.title: In development
bud.body: GitKittie Bud's macOS app isn't on the App Store yet, so there's nothing to install. Send a message to be told when it ships, or to say what you'd want from it.

mail.heading: GitKittie Mail
mail.title: In development
mail.body: GitKittie Mail isn't on the App Store yet, so there's nothing to install. Send a message to be told when it ships, or to say what you'd want from it.

setup.title: Adding an account, once it's out

steps.title: iCloud Mail
steps.desc: Mail never asks for your Apple Account password. Create an app-specific password at [account.apple.com](https://account.apple.com) under Sign-In and Security, and paste that.

steps.title: Any other IMAP account
steps.desc: Enter your address, the IMAP and SMTP servers and ports your provider lists, and your password or app password. Mail checks both servers before it saves anything, and says whether the password, the server, the certificate or the connection was the problem.

steps.title: A password that stopped working
steps.desc: If you change or revoke a password, the account stops syncing and says so. Use **Sign In Again** with the new one; your stored mail stays where it is.

stillStuck.title: Still stuck?
stillStuck.body: Send a message with the error text from Settings and your macOS version, and it arrives attached to the app it came from. Technical git output is kept in local logs, so sync errors can be diagnosed without exposing details in the menu bar.
